subject: English 1st Paper

source.edition: Revised for the year 2026; revised edition October 2025

passagePolicy: Read the cited textbook dialogues. They are separate situations, not one continuous passage; original questions below do not reproduce the full textbook.

activities.instruction: Read the cited dialogue and choose the best answer.

items.question: Where does Lily go to school?
items.explanation: The introductory situation places her school in Dhaka.

items.question: What result does Lily tell her father about?

options.B: An A in her English test

items.explanation: Lily reports her English test grade.

items.question: What kind of songs does Rahul enjoy singing?
items.explanation: The introduction describes his love of folk songs.

items.question: Why is Rahul happy?

options.C: He has won an essay prize
options.D: His new album has been a hit

items.explanation: His news concerns the success of an album of Lalon’s songs.

items.question: Which competition did Manzoor win?
items.explanation: The occasion was Independence Day and the event was an essay competition.

items.question: Why was Sujan absent from school?
items.explanation: Sujan says he had flu and spent most of the time in bed.

items.question: What does Manik think happened to his pen?
items.explanation: He is uncertain and says he thinks he dropped it somewhere.

activities.instruction: Answer from the cited dialogue. Equivalent accurate wording is acceptable.

items.question: Where do Lily’s parents live?
items.modelAnswer: They live in a small town in Tangail district.

items.question: How does Lily’s father react to her result?
items.modelAnswer: He praises her and says that he is proud of her.

items.question: Whose songs are on Rahul’s successful new album?
What class is Manzoor in, and what prize does he report winning?
items.modelAnswer: He is in class six and reports winning the first prize in the essay competition.

items.question: Why was the lost pen special to Manik?
items.modelAnswer: His father had given him the pen, and it was very dear to him.

items.question: What happened in Munira’s math test?
How does Shanu try to encourage Munira?
items.modelAnswer: Shanu says that her parents will understand and that she will do better next time.

activities.instruction: Give a suitable meaning in the dialogue, or a synonym where requested.

acceptedAnswers: people of approximately the same age
a collection of recorded songs or music
a very successful album in this context

activities.note: Hit means a popular success here, not a physical blow; dear expresses personal value, not necessarily high price. Album may have other meanings in other contexts.

activities.instruction: Write a kind and appropriate response to each situation. Model responses are examples, not the only correct wording.
activities.page: Language Focus and B2, printed 5–6 / PDF 10–11

items.question: A friend wins an essay prize.
A friend loses a football match.
items.modelAnswer: I’m sorry about the result. I hope your next match goes better.

items.question: Someone congratulates you on your result.
items.modelAnswer: Thank you! That is very kind of you.

items.question: A classmate tells you that they have been ill.
items.modelAnswer: I’m sorry to hear that. How are you feeling now?

items.question: A friend is selected for a television music programme.
items.modelAnswer: Congratulations! I’m very happy for you.

assessment: Responds appropriately to good news, bad news or thanks
Does not blame the person or promise an unverified outcome

activities.instruction: Write a dialogue congratulating a friend selected for a school music programme. Include a response to the congratulations and a natural ending.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rina
modelAnswer.text: Hello, Sami. You look happy. Do you have some good news?

modelAnswer.speaker: Sami
modelAnswer.text: Yes! I have been selected for our school music programme.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rina
modelAnswer.text: Congratulations! You have worked hard for this.

modelAnswer.speaker: Sami
modelAnswer.text: Thank you. Your encouragement means a lot to me.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rina
modelAnswer.text: When will the programme take place?

modelAnswer.speaker: Sami
modelAnswer.text: It will be next Thursday after our lessons.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rina
modelAnswer.text: Are you feeling ready to perform?

modelAnswer.speaker: Sami
modelAnswer.text: I am a little nervous, so I am practising every afternoon.

modelAnswer.speaker: Rina
modelAnswer.text: I hope it goes well. I look forward to hearing you sing.

modelAnswer.speaker: Sami
modelAnswer.text: Thanks, Rina. I am glad you will be there.

assessment: Supportive language without invented textbook claims
Clear speaker labels and comprehensible sentences
activities.note: Original writing model: Rina and Sami are fictional practice characters, not characters from the source dialogue. No official word limit or turn count is asserted.

limitations: Teacher review pending; this is a lesson pool rather than a full marked model test.
No poem appears in this lesson; no poem questions are padded into this pool.
Separate dialogue contexts must remain labelled when assembling exams.
The textbook describes a usual response to bad news, not a prohibition on speaking. Suitable supportive replies are accepted.
Practice is not exhaustive chapter-quota completion or website registration.
